words.definition: To perform or carry out; to act out or portray.
words.daily_usage: The actors enact the battle scene. / Congress will enact new environmental regulations.

words.definition: The principal front of a building, especially its most decorative or prominent face.
words.daily_usage: The museum's facade is made entirely of glass. / Workers restored the building's crumbling facade.
other_senses: (computing) a structural design pattern that provides a simplified, unified interface to a complex subsystem or body of code

words.definition: Expressing the same idea twice using different words; needlessly repetitive in meaning.
words.daily_usage: Free gift is a tautological phrase — a gift is already free by definition. / Saying past history is tautological since history is always in the past.
other_senses: (logic) always true by structure, regardless of content

words.definition: Double in amount or degree; twice as much or as many.
words.daily_usage: Sales grew twofold this year. / The plan has a twofold benefit — it saves time and money.
other_senses: having two distinct parts or elements

words.definition: A disordered jumble of things taking up space; mess.
words.daily_usage: There's too much clutter on my desk. / Build steps, tests and conventions might clutter a README.
other_senses: (verb) to fill or cover with untidy things

words.definition: A confused mixture of unrelated things thrown together.
words.daily_usage: A jumble of stationeries on the desk. / All of the concepts seemed to jumble together in my head.
other_senses: items for a rummage sale (British English)

words.definition: Impossible or very difficult to understand.
words.daily_usage: The lecture was full of jargon and completely incomprehensible to beginners.

words.definition: To be made up or composed of something.
words.daily_usage: The salad consists of lettuce, tomatoes, and cucumbers. / The team consists of five engineers.
other_senses: consist in — to have as the main/essential part (e.g., The beauty of the plan consists in its simplicity.)

words.definition: A subtle, delicate difference or distinction, especially in meaning, expression, or tone.
words.daily_usage: The two paintings are similar, but if you look closely you can appreciate the nuances. / He lacks social nuance — he can't read the room.
other_senses: (verb, less common) to treat or present with subtle distinctions — e.g., a nuanced argument

words.definition: With great care, dedication, and persistent effort.
words.daily_usage: She assiduously studied for the exam, going over every chapter twice. / He worked assiduously on the project for months.

words.definition: Steady persistence in doing something despite difficulties, obstacles, or discouragement.
words.daily_usage: Her perseverance through years of rejection finally paid off when she got published. / Learning a language takes patience and perseverance.

words.definition: A part, section, or segment into which something is divided or split.
words.daily_usage: The book is organized into three main divisions. / Each division of the company handles a different product line.
other_senses: act of dividing (e.g., division of labor)

words.definition: To convert something into its canonical (standard, preferred) form so equivalent values match and can be processed consistently.
words.daily_usage: We canonicalize URLs before caching them. / The import step canonicalizes field names to snake_case.
other_senses: to reduce an expression to a unique normal form (math/logic)
to put data into an official standard representation
